A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison; the substantial reformatting does not create material evidence gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical constructions, approximation guarantees, complexity bounds, and proofs. Appendix I contains an analytical memorization counterexample, not an original empirical experiment.

after.justification: V2 retains the theoretical study and analytical examples without adding experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results. References to empirical findings concern cited work.

M1.justification: The prompt-tuning objective, single-head single-attention-layer architectures, FFN depth–width alternatives, and low-rank inference approach are retained. The weight-construction proof revision is assessed under T1.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on concrete datasets or benchmarks. Lipschitz sequence-to-sequence functions and finite memorization datasets remain theoretical objects in both.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated experimental baselines. Comparisons with prior universality and memorization results remain theoretical; the additional citations do not introduce evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, budgets, metrics, or testing procedures. Model widths, prompt lengths, and norm bounds remain parameters of the theoretical analysis.

E4.justification: Appendix I retains the same attention decomposition and analytical prompt-tuning failure example. No ablation, robustness experiment, sensitivity study, or empirical case analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: No measured numerical or qualitative results are added, removed, or revised. The principal universality, memorization, and computational-complexity guarantees remain the same; the local proof revision is covered by T1.

T1.justification: Lemma D.2 replaces an exact normalization for an unspecified component with a lower bound on |p_1^T p'_1|. Its separation proof replaces the sum-of-absolute-values step with an argument selecting a dominant first term. This is a local mathematical revision; the main theorem statements and guarantees are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: universality with one attention head and layer, the FFN depth–width tradeoff, memorization capacity, and norm-dependent computational limits. V2's added concise summary restates these contributions.

C2.justification: Both retain the same normalization guidance, concerns about exponentially long prompts and information efficiency, and limitations for arbitrary pretrained transformers. The limitations paragraph moves to Appendix A.2 with abbreviated wording; Appendix I's mechanism explanation and failure conditions are unchanged.

D1.justification: No implementation, hardware, training, code, or data-access information is added or revised. V2's manuscript-update link and terminology clarifications provide no new implementation or reproducibility resources.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Alman and Yu (2024), Li et al. (2025), Kajitsuka and Sato (2025), and Zhou et al. (2025). Appendix A.1 also changes 'most similar to' Wang et al. into 'builds on' that work. These are limited attribution and positioning updates.

P1.justification: V2 copyedits prose and theorem statements, clarifies seq2seq terminology and TA/TB naming, and adds a concise summary. It removes the opening contents list, moves references before the appendices, and relocates limitations to Appendix A.2 while preserving the main narrative and proof organization.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts the ICLR conference layout, with smaller type, narrower text areas, recurring headers, compact spacing, and extensive reflow of theorem boxes and equations. The standalone title page becomes an integrated title–abstract–introduction page. Neither version contains result figures or tables.

improvement.justification: V2 provides modest readability and attribution gains through copyediting, clearer terminology, and updated references. Its scientific scope and principal guarantees remain unchanged. Lemma D.2 makes the intended dominant-term construction more explicit, but dominance alone does not justify its displayed exact equality, so a substantial improvement in theoretical rigor is not established.
